_comment: Fixture CV for the end-to-end test. Invented person, realistic shape. Deliberately contains one internal inconsistency (see `experience` vs the project durations) so the profile stage's proofreading has something to find.
position: Senior Backend Engineer | Python | Go | Kubernetes | AWS
experience: 8+ years in software development, backend and platform engineering

tech_summary.Cloud platforms: AWS (EKS, S3, RDS, Lambda, SQS), GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub)
tech_summary.Devops: Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Nginx, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD
tech_summary.Other: Distributed systems, API design, multi-tenancy, incident response, static analysis (some exposure via linter tooling)

projects.name: Multi-tenant CI analytics platform
projects.position: Senior Backend Engineer, then Tech Lead
projects.description: Owned the ingestion and query platform that processed build and test telemetry for around 400 customer organisations. Inherited a single-tenant Django monolith and moved it to a multi-tenant service on self-managed Kubernetes. Cut p99 query latency from 4.2 seconds to 380 milliseconds by restructuring the storage layer around ClickHouse while keeping PostgreSQL for everything transactional.
projects.stack: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS
responsibilities: Designed the tenant isolation model and the migration path off the shared schema
Chose PostgreSQL over a faster columnar store for the transactional path, for maintainability and hiring reasons
Ran the on-call rotation and wrote the runbooks after two multi-tenant data-leak near-misses
Introduced OpenTelemetry tracing before the migration, which is the only reason the cutover was debuggable
Reduced monthly infrastructure spend by 38% by right-sizing node pools and moving cold telemetry to S3

projects.name: Developer tooling and pre-commit static analysis
projects.description: Built and maintained the internal linting and pre-commit tooling used across roughly 120 repositories. Wrote custom AST-based rules in Python to catch unsafe database access patterns before review, and drove the false-positive rate down from 31% to under 6% over two quarters, which is what finally got engineers to stop disabling it.
projects.stack: Python, libcst, pre-commit, GitHub Actions, Docker
responsibilities: Authored custom AST rules and the framework other teams extended
Instrumented rule hit rates so noisy rules could be found and retired
Ran the rollout across teams, including the part where people hated it

projects.name: Payments reconciliation service
projects.description: Rebuilt the nightly reconciliation job as an event-driven service. Introduced idempotency keys after a retry storm double-charged 1,900 accounts, and that invariant is still the thing I check for first in any pipeline that touches money.
projects.stack: Python, Celery, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS
responsibilities: Designed the idempotent write path and the replay tooling
Wrote the postmortem and the guardrails that followed it
